rationale: Operator ruling 2026-10-31 via decision rubric (planner session), supersedes escalation DEC-0286 whose options retire-leaf and new-patch-id were both rejected. Problem: v6 signs every leaf of the patch-id file and the verifier refuses any non-approved leaf, so an in-place fix reviewed again on the same patch-id cannot be signed even when every reviewer's current verdict approves. Ruling: the credited leaf is the newest per (reviewer, patch-id); older leaves stay signed in the Merkle root and in the reviews ledger as superseded history. Matches Gerrit/GitHub latest-vote-per-reviewer and in-toto/Sigstore newest-statement-per-signer. Rejected: hand-retiring leaf[3] (edits signed evidence, sets a precedent) and a contrived new patch-id (evidence-shaping). Counter-argument weighed: every-leaf-approved is stricter, but a fresh patch-id already resets it for free, so it only penalises honest in-place fixes. Class: weakening of the every-leaf-approved control, operator-answered, not auto-applied; implemented by AISDLC-1144. AISDLC-1137 waits for it; no leaves file is edited.
